newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin set to win seat in parliament - poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin set to win seat in parliament - poll.

text.p: Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin is set to win the seat he is bidding for in France's snap parliamentary election even though he lost the last time he stood, an opinion poll showed on Tuesday.

The survey showed Jospin would win about 37 percent of the vote in the first round on May 25 and would win a seat in the run-off round on June 1 between the top scorers with between 55 and 60 percent of the vote.

Jospin, one of the rare French political leaders not in parliament, lost with 47.8 percent of the vote in the run-off round for the seat near this southwestern city when he stood at the last election in 1993.
The outgoing centre-right parliamentarian who defeated him, Jean-Pierre Bastiani, is not standing again and Jospin's main foe will be Marie-Denise Xerri, a centrist.
The poll was conducted last week among 501 local voters by the IPSOS firm. Jospin was first elected to parliament in Paris in 1981.
